Shared Informer - local cache of a resource, kept in sync via watch

Source: R/informer.R
Informer.Rd

Shared Informer - local cache of a resource, kept in sync via watch

Shared Informer - local cache of a resource, kept in sync via watch

Details

An Informer performs an initial list of a resource, then watches for subsequent changes and maintains a local cache keyed by namespace/name (or just name for cluster-scoped resources). Event handlers fire on add/update/delete.

This is the R equivalent of client-go's SharedIndexInformer. Informers are the canonical way to build controllers: one watch feeds many handlers and many Lister views, without each consumer re-listing the API server.

Lifecycle:

  • $run(stop_seconds = NULL) - block, streaming events into the cache. Returns when stop_seconds of wall-clock time elapse (whether or not events arrive) or $stop() is called from a handler. Safe to re-invoke; the informer resumes from the last observed resourceVersion.

  • $start(), then $poll(max_wait) in your own loop, then $close() - the same work without blocking, so one process can drive several informers (and other work) from a single loop. poll() handles events that have arrived, firing handlers, and returns.

  • On 410 Gone (the watch fell too far behind), the informer re-lists and reconciles the cache against the fresh list: objects that disappeared fire on_delete, new ones on_add, and changed ones (different resourceVersion) on_update.

  • Lists are fetched in pages of page_size items (limit/continue).

  • $has_synced() - TRUE once the initial list has been absorbed.

  • $lister() - return a Lister view over the current cache snapshot.

Public fields

client

The backing ApiClient.

resource_path

Path template (no {namespace}/{name} unresolved).

object_from_list

Optional constructor function(list) -> R6; when supplied, cached objects are R6 instances. Otherwise raw lists.

resource_version

Last observed resourceVersion (used to resume).

Register event handlers.

on_add

Function function(obj).

Method start()

List (unless the cache is already in sync) and open the watch, without blocking. Follow with $poll().

Usage

Informer$start()

Method poll()

Handle the events that have arrived, firing handlers. Starts the informer if needed. After a 410 Gone it re-lists, reconciles the cache and re-opens the watch.

Usage

Informer$poll(max_wait = 0)

Arguments

max_wait

Seconds to wait when nothing is pending (default 0).

Returns

The number of watch events handled, invisibly.

Method close()

Close the watch opened by $start() / $poll(). The cache is kept; a later $start() resumes from the last resourceVersion.

Usage

Informer$close()

Method run()

Run the informer: list (or resume), notify handlers, then watch until stop_seconds elapse or $stop() is called.

Usage

Informer$run(stop_seconds = NULL)

Arguments

stop_seconds

Optional wall-clock limit. NULL runs until $stop() is called from an event handler.

Make a running $run() return. Call from an event handler.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
client <- new_client_from_config()
inf <- Informer$new(
  client,
  resource_path = "/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods",
  object_from_list = V1Pod$from_list
)
inf$add_event_handler(
  on_add    = function(obj) message("add: ", obj$metadata$name),
  on_update = function(old, new) if (!identical(old$status, new$status))
                                   message("status change on ", new$metadata$name),
  on_delete = function(obj) message("gone: ", obj$metadata$name)
)
inf$run(stop_seconds = 30)

# Or drive it yourself, e.g. alongside other informers:
inf$start()
repeat inf$poll(1)

pods <- inf$lister()
pods$get("nginx")
pods$list()
} # }
